name: Polar's own scheme (747-400F)
description: Fuselage: All white. Titles: 'Polar' in big heavy blue italic letters on the forward fuselage, a thin red line running through the middle of the letters. Cheatlines: a thin dark-blue pinstripe from behind the title back along the side toward the tail. Tail: dark blue fin with Polar's mark, a white disc with a blue 'P' inside a ring of curved segments. Winglets: blue with the small mark. Engines: white.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Polar Air Cargo
sources.note: Fleet: six 747-400Fs from 2000, retired 2022 and redelivered to DHL; DHL's 49% stake announced October 2006.

history: Polar's own scheme on its 747-400Fs (N450PA to N454PA). From around 2008, after DHL took its 49% stake, most were repainted in the Polar/DHL co-brand (PAC/standard); N450PA kept this scheme until at least August 2018 and was in Atlas Air paint by September 2021. Polar's last 747-400Fs left in 2022 (Wikipedia).
notes: Drawn from N453PA (left, 2005) and N450PA (right, undated; Narita 2018). The 747's upper deck isn't in the shapes, so the title sits on the main fuselage's outline at its measured height. 'to' is when the last airframe seen in it (N450PA) was in other paint; it's approximate. Earlier Polar fleets (747-100/200Fs) aren't covered. Re-checked 2026-11-15: 'Polar' lowercase 0.71 of the capital (as measured on the current scheme's identical wordmark, N857GT 2024).
